strips.hook: [device: garbage-is-the-signal] [target: customers and prospects | form: solo monologue + silent witness (escalating list) | aim: outward | mechanic: anti-work-equilibrium (a rigorous, proud theory that actually holds) | cast: Maren + Susie, no protagonist] The gated price list collects forty invented names a day. Maren's operating rule: inventing a name costs effort, so the fakes are the only intent signal and the plausible entries are bots, a competitor and colleagues — she hands the SDR a dialling order and 'A. Sdf' is at the top.
strips.caption: Nobody has ever typed a real name into a download form. Your marketing team knows. Your marketing team has opinions about which fakes are worth calling.

strips.hook: [device: engineered-error] [target: cross-functional friction | form: two-hander | aim: lateral | mechanic: perverse-incentive-harvest | cast: Susie+Maren] Marketing catches a wrong stat in Susie's follow-up to a silent prospect. The error is the instrument: a prospect who can ignore a question cannot ignore a mistake, so every email she sends has exactly one number wrong.
strips.caption:
You cannot make a prospect answer you. You can make them correct you.

Susie's follow-ups all have exactly one thing wrong with them. Marketing found out this morning.

strips.hook: [device: protected-label] [target: meetings | form: two-hander | aim: systemic | mechanic: illusion-demolition | cast: Susie+Milo] Milo blocks two hours a day to prospect and it is moved every day; Susie's identical two hours have been untouched since March, because her calendar entry names an account instead of the work. She hands him the label, not a complaint.
strips.caption:
Don't name the work. Name the account.

strips.hook: [device: label-arbitrage] [target: cross-functional friction | form: two-hander | aim: lateral | mechanic: perverse-incentive-harvest (a respected LABEL is manufactured, not a metric) | cast: Maren+Susie — no Cal, no HOBS, no authority figure] In a sales company the only immovable calendar object is a customer, so marketing's real writing hour is booked as a customer call. Radar seed: HN 'Prevent cognitive debt by manually retyping LLM-generated code' (403 up / 342 comments) — thematic only (deliberately protecting slow work from a system that erodes it); Reddit was unreachable in today's radar, so no confessed-behavior calendar thread was available.

[device: proof-by-page-count] [target: customers and prospects | form: two-hander | aim: outward | mechanic: anti-work-equilibrium | cast: Susie+Maren] Marketing's twelve-page quarterly report has never been read — because the champion's only use for it is as an attachment proving the evaluation is alive, so the rep who owns the account asks for it LONGER, not better. Seeded by the Lenny's practitioner thread where operators confess how they manufacture reasons to stay on a stalled client's radar (pilot purgatory); works with all news deleted.

[device: process-recursion] [target: bureaucratic process | form: two-hander | aim: systemic | mechanic: policy-as-punchline | cast: Milo+Frank] The cheap purchase is the slow one — the fix is to spend more. Standalone; references nothing outside its own three panels. Scored 29/30 by independent craft judges in two separate rounds and passed the cold-scroller gate in both.

[device: compliance-laundering] [target: vendors & procurement | form: two-hander | aim: outward | mechanic: weaponised-literalism | cast: Frank+Susie] Susie needs a $1,240 tool only one vendor makes. The three-quote rule looks unsatisfiable without lying — so Frank, who enforces it, tells her to ask the vendor she already chose for its own competitor sheet: two real names, priced to lose.
strips.caption:
One vendor makes it. Three quotes required.
